title: Beyond Code Coverage: Functionality Testing with Playwright MCP — Marlene Mhangami, Microsoft
talk_summary: Marlene argues AI-generated code amplifies entropy unless codebases have strong behavioral tests, and proposes red-green TDD with Playwright functional tests instead of unit-coverage-only testing. She demos Playwright MCP/agents (planner, generator, healer) letting coding agents write failing browser tests, implement, run headless tests, and attach screenshots to PRs.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use Playwright MCP so an agent drives a real browser through user flows against the app, validating functionality rather than only unit coverage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Playwright is an open-source testing framework that's built by Microsoft and it automates end-to-end testing in the browser by simulating user interactions.

takeaways.technique: Red-green TDD with failing Playwright tests
takeaways.what_they_do: On a feature request, the agent first writes a failing behavioral Playwright test, then writes code to make it pass, then refactors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: writing the Playwright tests that fail for each feature

takeaways.what_they_do: Playwright agents install three agent.md roles: a planner that plans tests, a generator that writes tests, and a healer that fixes tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the first one is going to be a planner, second is a generator, and the third is a healer.

takeaways.what_they_do: Playwright captures screenshots of test runs, and the speaker adds them to PRs as functional evidence for reviewers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to take screenshots of all the tests that it's run. I've gotten into the practice of adding those screen screenshots to a PR.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run Playwright in headless mode so browser tests execute in the background without launching a visible browser.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can run it in headless mode, so that it runs in the background.

takeaways.what_they_do: Commit code before letting the agent fix tests, so the agent can recover prior state and avoid losing context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: commit before it starts to make changes to your code because if you don't commit, it might not remember
